result.topic_en: A calculation of a sum of products of sawtooth functions ((x)) (Dedekind-sum type expression), splitting into a first part that vanishes and a second part reducing to a sum 'as in Riemann'.
result.transcription:
II 3. $2\pi i \Big( \sum_{1,n-1} ((\frac{t}{n}-\frac{1}{2}))((\frac{mt}{n}-\frac{1}{2})) - 4\sum_{1,n-1} ((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac{1}{2}))((\frac{m+n}{2n}t-\frac{1}{2})) \Big)$
$2((\frac{t}{2n}-\frac{1}{2})) = ((\frac{t}{n}-\frac{1}{2})) - \frac{1}{2} \quad (t<n)$
$= 2\pi i \sum_{1,n-1} ((\frac{t}{n}-\frac{1}{2}))\{((\frac{mt}{n}-\frac{1}{2})) - 2((\frac{m+n}{2n}t-\frac{1}{2}))\} + 2\pi i \sum_{1,n-1}((\frac{m+n}{2n}t-\frac{1}{2}))$
erster Theil. $2.((\frac{m+n}{2n}t-\frac{1}{2})) = ((\frac{mt}{n}-\frac{1}{2})) \pm \frac{1}{2} \qquad \pm \pi i((\frac{m+n}{2n}t-\frac{1}{2}))$
$= \mp\pi i \sum_{1,n-1}' \pm ((\frac{t}{n}-\frac{1}{2})) = 0$
zweiter Theil. $t=2t,\ n-2t$
$2\pi i \sum_{1,\frac{n-1}{2}} \{((\frac{mt}{n}+\frac{1}{2})) - ((\frac{mt}{n}))\}$ wie bei Riemann.

methods.what: Halving relation for the sawtooth function used to rewrite the sum
Decomposition of the Dedekind-type sum into two parts
Second part reduced by substitution t=2t, n-2t to a half-range sum
